user: Once I have zeroed in on a house of my choice, what steps are involved in buying that property?
assistant: Once you've found the house you want to buy, the steps involved are:
 1. Work with your agent to put together and sign a purchase agreement. Make sure the sales contract includes the "VA escape clause" or "VA option clause," which provides an option to void the contract if the property doesn’t appraise for the contract price.  Now is also the time to start exploring loan choices and meeting with lenders.  Get official loan offers from lenders, compare your options, and choose the loan offer that's right for you.
2. Have the house inspected and appraised. It's recommended to get an inspection to check for any major defects before you purchase your home. A VA-approved appraiser will also appraise the house to ensure it meets basic property condition requirements and provide an opinion of value on the house.
3. If the property doesn’t appraise at a value that’s high enough to get the loan, you can request a Reconsideration of Value (ROV).
user: any public assistance for Vets?
assistant: Yes, there are various programs and benefits available for veterans. In terms of home loans, the VA provides VA Home Loans which include Purchase & Cash-Out Refinance Loan, Interest Rate Reduction Refinance Loan, and Native American Direct Loan among others. There are also mortgage assistance and foreclosure avoidance programs. 
user: How many years of work history needed to get a mortgage?
assistant: I do not have specific information regarding the number of years of work history needed to get a mortgage. It is recommended to check with the lender for their specific requirements.

which one do you recommend to have a regular mortgage or VA backed mortgage?
[The End of Current Turn Question]

[The Start of Reference Answer]
As a helpful assistant, I cannot personally recommend one over the other, however, I can provide some information to help you make an informed decision.
A VA-backed mortgage often offers advantages such as no down payment, better terms and interest rates, and no need for private mortgage insurance (PMI). These benefits can make homeownership more accessible and affordable for eligible veterans and service members.
On the other hand, a regular mortgage from a private lender may have different terms and requirements.  
Unfortunately I do not have information for  a traditional mortgage.  Consulting with a trusted financial advisor or mortgage professional can help you determine the best choice based on your personal situation.
[The End of Reference Answer]
